metadata.title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek-V4] Backport vllm-project/vllm#51856, #51262, #54838, #55954, #56141, #56271: prompt rendering and DSML tool parsing
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Backport of six upstream vLLM fixes for DeepSeek-V4 prompt rendering and DSML tool-call parsing, one commit each, in the same form as the earlier backports #657 (vllm-project/vllm#44082) and #1406 (vllm-project/vllm#60472). main does not have them. All six change frontend code only: the DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer wrapper and encoder (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py, vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py; tokenizer_mode auto selects deepseek_v4 for DeepseekV4ForCausalLM in vllm/config/model.py) and the DSML base parser vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv32_tool_parser.py, which the deepseek_v4 and deepseek_v41 tool parsers inherit. Nothing in it depends on the GPU, so DeepSeek-V4-Flash served on V100 or Turing with tools or a system prompt is affected like on any other hardware.

1. vllm-project/vllm#51856 (2909ad8fa, by Jason, thegoldenflow), "Attach request-level tools to existing system message in DeepSeek V4 Python renderer". With request-level tools, the tokenizer wrapper always inserted an extra empty system message in front of the conversation. A request with a system prompt and tools rendered as <BOS> + "\n\n## Tools ..." + system prompt, with the system prompt glued to the end of the tool block. DeepSeek's reference encoding puts the tools on the system message, which gives <BOS> + system prompt + "\n\n## Tools ...". The tools now attach to a copy of the first system message; a synthetic one is only added when none exists. Code and fixture hunks are applied unchanged; the updated tests/tokenizers_/fixtures/deepseek_v4/test_output_1.txt is byte-identical to encoding/tests/test_output_1.txt of the DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint. The new tests are appended by hand (upstream context did not match); their reference helper passes reasoning_effort="high" instead of "low", because this encoder accepts only None, "high" and "max" and the wrapper maps "low" to "high".

2. vllm-project/vllm#51262 (59d7fc92e, by Jiahao Liang), "Handle trailing system messages in prompt rendering". The encoder appended the <｜Assistant｜> transition only after user and developer messages. A system message followed by an assistant message glued the assistant text to the system text without a role token, and a trailing system message left the prompt without a generation start. Clients that compress a long history into a system summary followed by the remaining turns produce the first shape whenever the remaining turns start with an assistant message. The Python encoder hunk is applied unchanged. The three upstream tests are inserted by hand (context differs), plus one test for that compressed-history shape (system, system, assistant, user).

3. vllm-project/vllm#54838 (300f68832, by Flora Feng), "Implicitly close DeepSeek DSML parameters". When the model omits </｜DSML｜parameter>, the batch regex matched lazily up to the next parameter's close tag and the stream waited for a close tag only, so the next parameter ended up inside the previous value and was lost as a parameter (upstream issue #53227). Upstream changes its ParserEngine (vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py), which this repository does not have, so the intent is ported to DeepSeekV32ToolParser: the opener of the next parameter, '<｜DSML｜parameter name=', ends a value as well. In batch this is a lookahead in parameter_complete_regex; in the stream the earlier of close tag and next opener ends the value while a split opener is held back. The stream side is the implicit close that upstream added to its engine later (#58780). As upstream, whitespace before the next opener stays in the value.

4. vllm-project/vllm#55954 (d98c8c030, by Flora Feng), "Parse DSML tool calls when the model omits the tool_calls wrapper". At long context DeepSeek-V4-Flash sometimes omits <｜DSML｜tool_calls> and opens <｜DSML｜invoke ...> directly (upstream issue #48931). The parser only looked for the wrapper, so the whole block reached the client as text and no tool call happened, in batch and stream. Ported to the same parser: the invoke opener starts the tool calls like the wrapper does. Batch parses every complete invoke from the first of the two markers on, and content is the text before that marker. In the stream, once tool calls have started, wrapper tokens are consumed and text between or after the blocks is dropped, holding back possibly split markers. As upstream, this changes one existing behaviour: text after a closed tool-calls block is no longer streamed as content; the batch path dropped it already. The unused wrapper-block regex is removed. The upstream test changes for test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py apply unchanged; added tests cover a preamble plus trailing text, with and without the closing wrapper, and a wrapped block after an orphan invoke, each in batch and stream.

5. vllm-project/vllm#56141 (9e2570656, by Flora Feng), "Tolerate misspelled DSML tool_calls wrapper". DeepSeek-V4-Flash intermittently writes the opener as <｜DSML｜toolcalls> or <｜DSML｜tool> (upstream issue #51914), and the deepseek_v4 parser leaked it into the content. Upstream extends its ParserEngine terminals and lexer; here the two observed spellings are a class attribute tool_call_start_token_variants of DeepSeekV4ToolParser (empty in the base class), and the base parser treats every listed opener like the real one in batch and stream. Only these spellings count; other <｜DSML｜...> text stays content. Upstream's reasoning-side part (a misspelled opener inside the reasoning ends it like the real one) has no counterpart here, because the deepseek_v4 reasoning parser (DeepSeekV3ReasoningParser) does not end reasoning at the real wrapper either.

6. vllm-project/vllm#56271 (39e33db7f, by lazymio, wtdcode), "Fix the parsing of missing string= in DeepSeek V4". The DSML regexes required string="true|false" on every parameter. When the model omits the attribute, batch parsing dropped the parameter and the stream never matched the opener, so the client got a tool call without arguments. Upstream changes its ParserEngine converter. Ported here: one shared parameter head pattern for the batch and stream regexes with an optional string attribute, and a missing attribute counts as string="false", so the tool schema decides the type as for any non-string value (upstream: JSON first, then the literal).

Fixes 3 to 6 make the parser accept malformed model output, as upstream does. The model output is external data the server does not control, each shape is reported upstream with samples, and without the tolerance the tool call is lost or its arguments are wrong. Well-formed output is parsed as before; the V3.2 and V4.1 parsers inherit 3, 4 and 6 with their own tag names.

The Rust renderer and parser parts of the upstream PRs (#51262, #56271) are not included; the Python server path is fixed.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs of this repository for 51856, 51262, 54838, 55954, 56141, 56271, DSML, "DeepSeek V4 tool parser", "deepseek_v4 renderer", "system message tools DeepSeek", deepseekv32_tool_parser, "tool_calls wrapper", "missing parameter close", "string= DSML", misspelled and "trailing system message", and the issues for DSML and the six numbers. No PR backports these fixes; #842 (merged) handles a missing parameter close in the Qwen XML parser, a different parser. Issue #597 reports malformed DSML tool calls from DeepSeek-V4-Flash on V100; I have not checked whether these fixes change its result.

AI assistance was used for this backport. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv41_tool_parser.py
The same test files against main's sources (git checkout origin/main -- vllm/ in the branch, then back).
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
End to end on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, prod-v6f 0b342e7b5, which carries these six commits; DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 over three V100 and two RTX 8000 with --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4, temperature 0): a request with a system prompt and a get_weather tool, non-streaming and streaming; a conversation system, system, assistant, user; a trailing system message after an assistant turn.

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer wrapper (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4.py) | chat prompt rendering | request-level tools, with or without a system message | tools on a copy of the first system message; a synthetic system message only when none exists | executed: tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py, including golden fixture 1 | deepseek_v41 tokenizer not touched |
| DeepSeek-V4 encoder (vllm/tokenizers/deepseek_v4_encoding.py) | chat prompt rendering | system message last, or followed by an assistant message | <｜Assistant｜> transition appended, thinking token as for a user turn | executed: tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py | Rust renderer not changed |
| DSML tool parsers deepseek_v4, deepseek_v41, deepseek_v32 (vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv32_tool_parser.py and subclasses) | tool calls, batch and streaming | missing parameter close, missing tool_calls wrapper, misspelled wrapper (deepseek_v4 only), missing string attribute | calls parsed as from well-formed output; unregistered DSML text stays content | executed: tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py, test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py, test_deepseekv41_tool_parser.py | Rust tool parser not changed; the malformed shapes were not provoked on a live model (its tool call was well-formed) |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fix, not a performance change.
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664; the same commits run on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, prod-v6f at 0b342e7b5).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none for the tests.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. The fork tree with these six commits and the other upstream backports of the same bundle passed an A/B/A/B (test, production, test, production) of our DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 entry against the tree without them: prefill 2.28 s for an 8921-token prompt in all four arms, short decode 55.87 to 55.88 tok/s, GSM8K-30 29 of 30 in all arms, eight quality texts token-identical, a 486,316-token prompt served in both a test and a production arm.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these six commits):
- tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py and the three DSML parser test files: 113 passed.
- The same tests against main's sources: tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py 9 failed (the five #51262 cases and the four #51856 cases, among them golden fixture 1); test_deepseekv32_tool_parser.py and test_deepseekv41_tool_parser.py pass on both. test_deepseekv4_tool_parser.py does not collect against main, because one parametrization reads DeepSeekV4ToolParser.tool_call_start_token_variants; with the two spellings written out in the test, 13 of its 23 tests fail on main (the cases for #54838, #56141 and #56271 and those for #55954, including the two upstream test changes) and pass on this branch; the added check that unregistered DSML markup stays content passes on both.
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes except check-layering, which reports vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py (platform coupling 25 -> 32) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py (37 -> 39); this PR touches neither file, the report is the same on main c98a8d664.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.

End to end on our fork as in the test plan: the system prompt plus tool request returns finish_reason tool_calls with get_weather {"city": "Hamburg", "days": 3}, and the streamed request the same call and arguments. The system, system, assistant, user conversation is answered as the user's turn ("Die Strecke von Hamburg nach Lübeck beträgt auf dem Radweg entlang von Alster und Stecknitz etwa 60 bis 65 Kilometer."), and the trailing system message as a new turn ("Der Eiffelturm ist das bekannteste Wahrzeichen von Paris ..."). This shows the changed paths on the GPU build; the before and after difference is in the CPU tests above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_0172gtUn2th65t88H9KvYkwK
